title: Introduce pulse sampler and adaptive metric retention for SLO investigations
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Investigations into SLO regressions often require high-fidelity traces and short-lived metric retention for a small set of problematic routes, which is expensive at full cardinality. This PR introduces a lightweight "pulse sampler" that can be toggled per-route (or globally) to temporarily increase telemetry fidelity for affected invocations, plus an adaptive retention controller that shortens raw-timeseries TTLs for metrics that are only needed during incident windows.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a pulse-sampler component in the serving runtime to attach a small high-priority trace + detailed token-phase metrics for sampled invocations. Pulse samples are limited by a budget and decay automatically.
- Implements an adaptive-metric-retention controller that: 1) marks metric families as "investigation" when a pulse sample occurs, 2) sets a short high-resolution retention policy (e.g., 7d@1s) for those families, and 3) automatically rolls them back after an inactivity window.
- Exposes an operator API and console flag (SLO investigator mode) to trigger manual pulses and view currently elevated retention families.
- Adds a compact dashboard (slo-investigator.json) that surfaces pulse frequency, retained metric sets, and estimated storage delta.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The sampler captures only a constrained subset of data (callsite, token-phase timings, small KV cache deltas, top-3 logits for degen debugging) to bound per-invocation cost. It does not send full logs or request/response bodies.
- The retention controller operates at metric-family granularity to avoid explosion of retention rules per tag. We intentionally bias towards low-cardinality families (route, model, deployment).
- Budgeting: pulse budget is configurable per-tenant and enforced by a token-bucket in the control-plane; pulses beyond budget are logged and dropped.

Migration and rollout:
- Default behavior is gated behind feature flag observability.pulse_sampler=false. The console UI and API can enable investigator mode per-tenant.
- Rolling update plan: enable sampler on Canary (internal accounts) for 48h, validate storage impact on metrics cluster, open canary to a subset of customers, then enable off by default with opt-in.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for sampler decision logic and controller TTL lifecycle.
- Integration test that simulates an incident, triggers pulses, verifies retention rules applied and then removed after cooldown.
- Load validation: microbenchmarks show ~1-3% CPU overhead on hotpath when sampler is active at 1% sampling rate.

Backwards compatibility: Adds new config knobs but preserves existing metric ingestion semantics when feature is disabled.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation in runtime and control plane
- [x] Console UI + dashboard
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs (observability/pulse-sampler.md)
- [x] Canaries validated

Related: ENG-3412 (SLO investigation workflow), ENG-3499 (metric retention controls).

review_conversation: Ethan Cole (review): Overall looks good. Two asks: (1) make the default pulse payload smaller (drop logits) and (2) add a safety cap if many routes are pulsing at once to avoid overwhelming retention controller.
Author (Ava): Dropped logits from default payload, added per-shard safety cap and documented fallback behavior in controller.go (commit c7d9e10).
Priya Nair (review): Can you add a metric to expose current pulse budget usage per-tenant? Helps SRE correlate stored retention with budget burns.
Author (Ava): Added telemetry/metrics pulse_budget_used_total (gauge) and increment points - see pulse_sampler.go. Updated integration test to assert metric emission.
Luca Moretti (review): Console UX: please add a confirmation dialog for manual investigator toggles and a soft-rate-limit in the UI to prevent mass toggles.
Author (Ava): Added confirmation modal and client-side debounce.

release_notes:
- Experimental: Pulse sampler for high-fidelity short-lived telemetry (opt-in)
- Adaptive metric retention controller to shorten TTLs for investigation-only metric families
- Console: SLO Investigator toggle and dashboard showing pulse activity and storage impact
Notes: Feature is off by default. Follow the rollout guide in docs/observability/pulse-sampler.md.
summary: Adds an opt-in pulse sampler and retention controller to enable targeted high-resolution telemetry during SLO investigations while limiting storage impact.
